tasks.title: Thread the resolved dataDir instead of reconstructing paths
tasks.description:
Two sites rebuild a hardcoded '.ralph' path segment instead of using the dataDir already in scope. Under the dual-read fallback added in task 31, discovery may resolve '.ralph/' while BRAND.dataDir says '.cairn' — so these reconstructions will point at the wrong directory.

1. src/index.ts:127 — `completedTasksPath: join(projectRoot, '.ralph', 'tasks.completed.json')` in the summarize action. Use the resolved dataDir.
2. src/post-task-reviewer.ts:137 — `const reviewFileRule = `/${projectRoot}/.ralph/reviews/**`` which becomes the Edit/Write permission allowlist rule for the reviewer subagent. Use the resolved dataDir.

The second is the dangerous one. If the reviewer is granted an allowlist for '.cairn/reviews/**' while the project is actually on '.ralph/', every reviewer write is SILENTLY DENIED — no error, reviews just vanish. That exact failure mode was the subject of a previous round's fix; do not reintroduce it.

TDD: write a failing test asserting that a project whose data dir resolves to legacy '.ralph/' produces an allowlist rule pointing at '.ralph/reviews/**', and that a '.cairn/' project produces '.cairn/reviews/**'. Then make it pass.
tasks.notes:
# Task #32 — Thread the resolved dataDir instead of reconstructing paths

## What changed

**`src/index.ts`**
- `setupProjectContext()` line 36: `join(projectRoot, '.ralph')` → `findDataDir(projectRoot)`. This is the *root* of the threading: `RALPH_DATA_DIR` (and therefore every downstream `dataDir` in the CLI, including the one handed to the post-task reviewer) now comes from discovery instead of a literal. Without this the two named sites would have been cosmetic no-ops — everything downstream was still hardcoded `.ralph`.
- summarize action line ~127: `join(projectRoot, '.ralph', 'tasks.completed.json')` → `join(dataDir, 'tasks.completed.json')` using the `dataDir` already in scope.

**`src/post-task-reviewer.ts`** (`spawnPostTaskReviewer`)
- Added `const absDataDir = path.resolve(projectRoot, dataDir)` and built `reviewsDir` from it. Permission rules require an absolute path; resolving against `projectRoot` makes a relative `dataDir` safe too. `path.resolve` on an already-absolute `dataDir` just normalizes it, so real callers are unaffected.
- `reviewFileRule` is now `` `/${reviewsDir}/**` `` instead of `` `/${projectRoot}/.ralph/reviews/**` ``. The allowlist grant and `reviewFilePath` are now derived from the *same* `reviewsDir` variable, so they are structurally incapable of naming different directories. The leading `/` (producing `//abs/path/...`) is the existing convention — kept deliberately, see the comment block.

**`CLAUDE.md`** — the agent-workflow paragraph said the reviewer allowlist covers `.ralph/reviews/**`; now says `<dataDir>/reviews/**` and records *why* the rule must be derived from the resolved dir (silent denial, no error).

## Tests (TDD — written first, all 9 confirmed failing before the fix)

`test/post-task-reviewer.test.ts`, in `describe("spawnPostTaskReviewer")`:
- allowlist rule for a legacy `.ralph/` dataDir → `Edit(//<root>/.ralph/reviews/**)` (passed pre-fix; guards the legacy path against regression)
- allowlist rule for a `.cairn/` dataDir → `Edit(//<root>/.cairn/reviews/**)` (failed pre-fix — got `.ralph`)
- invariant test: the round file path in the prompt is a prefix-match under the allowlist rule's directory glob. This is the one that catches the *class* of bug rather than one instance of it.

`test/index.test.ts`:
- new `describe('data dir resolution')` under `setupProjectContext`: existing `.cairn/`, legacy-only `.ralph/`, neither (defaults `.cairn/`), both (prefers `.cairn/`).
- new `describe('summarize action')`: drives `main(['--project-root', tmp, 'summarize'])` with `spyOn(summarizeModule, 'runSummarize')` and asserts `completedTasksPath` lands under the resolved data dir, for both layouts.

**Technique worth reusing:** Bun's `spyOn(namespaceImport, 'exportedFn')` *does* intercept a live ESM binding that `src/index.ts` already imported — no `mock.module` needed. That makes any command action reachable through `main()` testable without adding dependency-injection seams. `mockRestore()` in a `finally` cleans up.

`bun test` → **765 pass, 0 fail** (28 files; was 756 before, +9 new).

## Build health check — the reported failure was stale, not real

The iteration banner reported a browser-target build error on `readline`. `ralph.json`'s `healthCheck` already carries `--target=bun` (added in task 31) and passes cleanly, as does `bun run build`. Cause: the long-lived `ralph run` parent process loaded `ralph.json` once at startup — *before* task 31 edited it mid-run — so it is still executing the old command string from memory. It will clear on the next `ralph run`. **No code fix needed; do not "re-fix" this.** (If it recurs on a freshly started run, that *would* be a real bug.)

## Carry-forward

The standing rule from task 31 still holds and is now enforced at the top of the chain: `BRAND.dataDir` is for CREATING paths, `findDataDir()` for RESOLVING them.

Remaining hardcoded `.ralph` in `src/` after this task — all intentional, all owned by task 33 (`.ralph_` *temp-file prefix*, a separate naming tier from the directory name):
- `src/task-archiver.ts:63` `.ralph_completed_ids`, `:81` `.ralph_prev_notes`
- `src/tasks-file.ts:130,191` `.ralph_tasks_snapshot.json`
- `src/task-selector.ts:9` `.ralph_completed_ids`

No non-comment `.ralph` *directory* literals remain in `src/`.

Not touched (out of scope, owned by later tasks): `RALPH_*` env var names (task 35), `src/commands/edit.ts` config path (task 37/40), `src/commands/init.ts` creation sites (task 37).

tasks.title: Stateful temp files: .cairn_ prefix with .ralph_ dual-read
tasks.description:
There is a second naming tier INSIDE the data dir: runtime temp files prefixed '.ralph_', independent of the directory name. Four of them carry live cross-run state, so switching writes to '.cairn_' without a read fallback would SILENTLY DISCARD that state:

- .ralph_completed_ids — read at src/task-selector.ts:9, written at src/task-archiver.ts:63
- .ralph_prev_notes — the PREV_NOTES cross-iteration mechanism, src/task-archiver.ts:81
- .ralph_iterations.log — src/commands/logs.ts:5 and src/commands/run.ts:361
- .ralph_tasks_snapshot.json — corruption recovery, src/tasks-file.ts:130 and :191

Also handle .ralph_complete (src/commands/run.ts:47, :420 and the TEMP_FILES array at :354).

Pattern: WRITE with the '.cairn_' prefix; READ trying '.cairn_' first and falling back to '.ralph_'.

Also update the notes-sweep regex at src/commands/run.ts:689 from /^\.ralph_task_\d+_notes\.md$/ so it matches BOTH prefixes — otherwise old scratch files linger forever.

Do NOT rename the .ralph_task_*_notes.md files themselves or change how they are written. They are write-and-sweep scratch, never read back, and 24 of them are committed history in another project.

TDD: explicitly test the fallback read path for each of the four stateful files — that is the whole point of the task.

tasks.title: Dual-name build and install
tasks.description:
package.json: change "name" to "cairn" and the build script outfile from dist/ralph to dist/cairn.

install.sh: symlink BOTH ~/.local/bin/cairn AND ~/.local/bin/ralph to dist/cairn. Rename the internal shell vars RALPH_ROOT/RALPH_BIN to CAIRN_ROOT/CAIRN_BIN (these are local to the script, never exported). Update echo messages.

The 'ralph' symlink is a LONG-LIVED compatibility commitment, not a deprecation stub: four other projects on this machine have `ralph task ...` frozen into their installed .claude/agents/*.md copies, and they break the moment it stops resolving. Do not add a deprecation warning that fires on every invocation.

CRITICAL — do NOT run ./install.sh, and do NOT modify ralph.json's healthCheck value. For the duration of this round the user has pinned ~/.local/bin/ralph to a frozen binary copy and redirected the health check to a throwaway outfile, specifically so that changing the build outfile here is inert. Both are user-managed and reverted manually after the loop finishes.

tasks.title: Env vars to CAIRN_* plus three-way API-key chain
tasks.description:
Rename the 22 RALPH_* env var names to CAIRN_*. Start with setConfigEnvVars() at src/config.ts:132-143, then every reader across src/ (index.ts, commands/*.ts, utils.ts). Note the comment at src/config.ts:130 claims these match 'ralph_config.sh for shell fallback compatibility' — that file does not exist anywhere in the repo. Delete the stale comment.

TWO EXCEPTIONS that need fallbacks, because they live outside every repo:

1. RALPH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — read at lib/ralph_narrate_server.py:222 as `os.environ.get("RALPH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY") or os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")`. This prefix is LOAD-BEARING: the main loop blanks ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (run.ts:203, plan.ts:170, summarize.ts:111, post-task-reviewer.ts:119) to force Max-plan usage, and the prefixed name is what still lets the narration server reach a real key. It is exported in the user's ~/.zshrc. Implement a three-way chain: CAIRN_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> RALPH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, warning when it lands on the legacy name. Never normalize it to plain ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
2. RALPH_NARRATE_SOCKET — user-facing, documented at README:161 for standalone claude sessions. Keep a fallback.

Delete RALPH_FORCE_SHELL entirely — it is dead, surviving only in a stale .claude/settings.local.json permission entry.

TDD: test the API-key chain resolution order explicitly.

tasks.title: cairn migrate command - core moves
tasks.description:
Create a new `migrate` command: src/commands/migrate.ts plus registration in src/index.ts. It converts one project from the .ralph/ layout to .cairn/.

BEHAVIOR (all settled decisions, do not re-litigate):
- Operates on the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY ONLY. No scanning for projects. Resolve the root via the same dual-read discovery as everything else, and exit with a clear error if cwd is neither a Cairn nor a Ralph project.
- Non-interactive and idempotent — running twice must be safe.
- PREFLIGHT: refuse to run if any task in tasks.json has status 'in-progress'; warn (do not refuse) if the git working tree is dirty.
- `git mv` the data dir (.ralph -> .cairn) and the config file (ralph.json -> cairn.json). Verified behavior: git mv on a directory renames it on the filesystem AND stages the tracked renames, so untracked and gitignored files come along automatically — a single git mv handles everything inside.
- Rename the four stateful temp files inside the data dir: .ralph_completed_ids, .ralph_prev_notes, .ralph_iterations.log, .ralph_tasks_snapshot.json -> .cairn_* equivalents.
- Leave .ralph_task_*_notes.md and ALL archive files (tasks.completed.json, reviews/round-*.md, audit/) completely untouched — they are historical record and must move unmodified.
- Tolerate partial installs: one target project has no state.json, no reviews/ dir, and no installed agents. Nothing may assume a complete layout.
- STAGES CHANGES, NEVER COMMITS. The user reviews before it lands.

TDD: test against a temp git fixture directory using `bun run src/index.ts migrate`, NOT the installed binary (which is pinned to a frozen build for this round and will not contain your new command).

tasks.title: cairn migrate - .claude refresh and git staging
tasks.description:
Extend the migrate command from task 43 to refresh installed artifacts and stage everything it touched.

1. Re-install agents and slash commands by reusing installAgents() and installSlashCommands() from src/commands/init.ts — they already overwrite via copyFileSync. Install the FULL current set even where none existed previously: one target project has zero installed agents and this is its upgrade path.
2. NON-DESTRUCTIVE RULE: overwrite by filename only. Never delete, never sync-and-prune, never touch files outside the source set. One target project has a custom .claude/agents/frontend-code-analyzer.md that must survive untouched.
3. Regenerate the three .claude/hooks/*.sh scripts for the new socket path — but ONLY if hooks already exist in that project. Do not create hooks where there were none.
4. Rewrite the data dir's .gitignore with both .cairn_* and .ralph_* prefixes, PRESERVING any custom lines the project added (one project appended 'instructions.md').
5. GIT STAGING: git mv stages itself, but everything else here does not. Explicitly `git add` all non-git-mv output — the rewritten .gitignore, regenerated hooks, and any newly installed agent/command files. Without this they sit unstaged, or for a project that never had them, entirely UNTRACKED — so the user would review an incomplete `git diff --cached` and think the migration was smaller than it was.
6. Finish by printing a `git status` style summary of exactly what was staged.

Must remain idempotent. TDD via temp git fixture using `bun run src/index.ts migrate`, not the installed binary.

3. docs/parallel-execution-rfc.md (9 references).

Also DOCUMENT THE NEW MECHANICS:
- The `cairn migrate` command: what it does, that it operates on cwd only, and that it stages without committing.
- The compatibility window: .cairn/ and .ralph/ are both read, cairn.json and ralph.json are both read, and both `cairn` and `ralph` binaries are installed. Explain that the ralph symlink stays until every project is migrated.
- The pin/unpin procedure for self-modifying rounds: because the health check is the build and it runs every iteration, renaming the tool while it runs requires freezing the installed binary and redirecting the health check to a throwaway outfile first. This is genuinely useful institutional knowledge for future rounds.

tasks.title: Verification sweep
tasks.description:
Final audit. Run `grep -rni ralph` across the repo, excluding .git/, node_modules/, dist/, .venv/, and the historical-record files.

Every surviving hit must fall into exactly one of two categories:
1. An INTENTIONAL compatibility fallback — dual-read discovery (.ralph/), config fallback (ralph.json), temp-file prefix fallback (.ralph_*), the RALPH_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and RALPH_NARRATE_SOCKET env chains, and the ralph symlink in install.sh.
2. A HISTORICAL RECORD file that must never be rewritten: .ralph/tasks.completed.json, .ralph/.ralph_iterations.log, .ralph/.ralph_tasks_snapshot.json, .ralph/reviews/round-*.md, .ralph_task_*_notes.md, audit/ contents, and .ralph/planning-notes.md.

Anything else is a miss from an earlier task — fix it.

Mark every fallback in category 1 with a comment: `// remove once all projects migrated` (or the language-appropriate equivalent). Six projects share this tool and five still use the .ralph/ layout; the removal round happens only after all are migrated, and these markers make it mechanical.

Report the final tally: how many references remain, and the category breakdown. bun test must pass.
